text: None of the four echoes a rival's look: the paint-by-number rows are all bright flowers, pixel hearts, pumpkins and easels, and no candidate uses a flower, heart grid or easel.
None of the four has visible paper grain or brush texture at 100%; every fill is vector-flat or gradient, so all of them could use a touch of handmade surface.
[#3]: the blobs have no ink edge while the circle does, so the two languages clash a little; giving the blobs a slight outline or merging them into regions would tighten it.

[#1]: a crescent with a bold 3 inside a dark outline stays readable in two tones, tinted at all three sizes and dimmed at night, but the crescent alone echoes several sleep apps (White Noise, Sleep Sounds) in the competitor row.
[#1]: its home-screen name 'Moonlight' fits without an ellipsis and the crescent-with-number stays legible at all three tinted sizes, the clearest single mark of the four.
In the two-tone view [#1] and [#2] keep a clear figure plus numeral, while [#4] fragments into stripes and stars and [#3] is just a disc; bold shapes hold, scenic detail does not.

[#3]: the full moon with purple patches reads, in the dimmed night view, as a lump with blotches; the patches look like paint spills more than a moon's face, so neither the hour nor the craft comes through cleanly.
[#3]: a full moon with blotchy maria on dark purple matches no rival in the rows shown; BetterSleep's moon is a white glow on a green hill, clearly different.

All four share the same cream paper, near-black ink and serif numerals, so the choice is about motif and finish rather than palette; the gradients of [#4] are the one break from the flat printed-template look.

[#1] is one crescent and one numeral on an empty field; in two tones it stays a clear crescent with its 3, and the dark around it is part of the work. It reads at all three tinted sizes and at night brightness.
[#1] and [#3] show 'Moonlight' as a short home-screen name that fits without truncation, unlike [#4].

[#2]: a cream ground with a big 6 by day that turns into a dark ground by night. This is the only icon that really changes with the hour, and the gold arc reads as a sun or a sunrise over hills, a gentle sign rather than clip art.

[#2]: the teal hill with its ochre sliver and the hand-drawn, wobbly ink outline around a big soft '6' look like a page from a garden almanac, and 'Paint by Heart' sounds like something made by hand. It reads as grown, not manufactured.
[#2]: the big '6' on cream hills is unlike any rival icon, but 'Paint by Heart' sits close to Paint Your World and the many heart icons in the color-by-number rows, and the icon shows no heart.
[#3]: one disc and one numeral, nothing to remove; the thin 4 is the weakest stroke and the dithered lower edge leaks into the white below.
None of the four is scary; nothing here frightens the way the rivals' grinning Halloween pumpkins do. [#4] and [#1] carry the moon-and-wonder story that the name 'Paint by Moonlight' promises.

[#2]: an amber sliver over a teal hill reads as sunrise or sunset, so the hour is unclear. The big 6 is the most legible numeral of the four, but 'Paint by Heart' has nothing to do with moonlight or the sky.

[#1]'s white crescent on dark navy looks almost the same as the sleep-sounds icons in the same sheet ('White Noise Deep...', 'Sleep Sounds - R...', 'Sleep: Sounds &...'), so in search it reads as a sleep app. The small '3' is the only thing that says painting.
[#3]: the moon is drawn as a paint-by-number shape with purple patches and a numeral '4' inside a cell, which no rival or sleep icon does; the moon becomes the canvas, so it is distinctly ours.

Every rival in the paint-by-number, color-by-number and coloring-book rows is a saturated flower, heart, pixel art or pumpkin on white, and no rival name avoids 'Paint/Color by Number'. All four muted, dark candidates and their names stand apart from that category at a glance.
[#3]: the purple splotches on the full moon look like paint patches. Next to the numeral that suggests painting by numbers, but at the smallest tinted size the patches turn to mush.
[#3]: the purple blotches on the full moon read as bruises or mold, not clouds, in the full-size crop and on the dim screen. A spotty moon feels a little eerie at bedtime.
[#1]: a lone crescent on dark navy sits right beside the sleep-sounds apps (White Noise, Sleep Sounds), so it reads as cold and like a sleep app, not something you paint with your hands.
[#3] and [#1] use the short home-screen name 'Moonlight', which fits without truncation but drops 'Paint', so on the home screen only the small numeral signals what the app does.
[#3]: lumpy, irregular purple blobs with no outline sit on cream like real paint dabs, the most hand-made texture in the set, and the crisp serif 4 inside an inked circle still says paint by numbers.

No name follows a famous order, house or council, and "Paint by Moonlight" / "Paint by Heart" appear nowhere in the rival names list. Avoid: drifting further toward the lone-crescent-on-navy sleep-app template, and any ® naming style like Happy Color® or ColorPlanet®.
[#4]: the stars and moon over hills are the most wonder-full scene, but the 4 shrinks to a speck at the middle size and vanishes at the smallest, so the icon stops saying painting by numbers.
[#3]: the purple blotches on the pale moon read as spots or bruises at night size, so the moon looks a little sick rather than friendly.

[#4] holds five stars, a glowing moon, three hills and a numeral; at the smallest tinted size the 4 is a speck and the stars are dust, so the one thing that says 'numbers' is the first to go. It is also the only name cut short on the home screen ('Paint by Mo...').
[#3]: the purple blobs on the full moon read as craters, not paint regions, and the dimmed and tinted views turn them into mottled noise around a small 4.
All four avoid the crowded flower-and-heart look of every paint-by-number rival, which is a real distinction; the moon candidates trade that for overlap with sleep and meditation apps.
[#3]: the purple blobs read as moon craters or splotches rather than paint regions, and in the two-tone view they disappear entirely, leaving a plain disc with a 4.
[#1]: a white crescent on dark navy sits almost exactly beside Sleep Sounds - R... and Sleep: Sounds & ... in the sleep row; the small '3' is the only thing separating it from a sleep app.

[#4]: the 4 is a tiny numeral at the bottom edge that vanishes at the smallest tinted size and on the home screen, and the label truncates to "Paint by Mo...", so neither icon nor name says paint-by-number on the phone.
[#4]: crescent and stars over purple dunes recalls the sleep icons (Sleep Sounds - R..., BetterSleep) more than painting, and its 4 is tiny; generic night imagery rather than borrowed from anyone.

[#2]: the 6 is big and stays clear at all three sizes, and the hills read as a filled region, so this is the most legible icon for low-vision users. The name 'Paint by Heart' sounds warm, but it suggests you need feeling or skill, which may not welcome someone who is just tapping numbers.

[#4]: a crescent and stars over purple hills sits close to the sleep row's night scenes (BetterSleep's moon over a green hill, Sleep Sounds - R...). Its tiny '4' is the only paint-by-number cue, and it nearly disappears.
[#2]: the deep teal is the only green-ish note among the four, a garden-at-dusk color that warms me, though the huge cropped 6 crowds the scene.
[#4]: the full night scene (stars, crescent, purple hills) spells the sky out instead of hinting at it, and its 4 shrinks to an unreadable dot at home-screen size.
[#1]: a big bright crescent holding a clear 3 on deep night is calm and easy to spot at a glance, and "Moonlight" fits under it whole.

[#1] and [#3] crescents and moons sit beside the sleep-sounds row in the competitor view (White Noise, Sleep Sounds), so the moon alone says 'sleep'; only the numeral says 'paint'. Keep the numeral large enough to survive the smallest size.

[#2]: the big 6 survives every test, including the smallest tinted size and the bedtime dim view, but the dark-mode version is nearly black, and 'Paint by Heart' loses the moon story the other three share.
[#1]: a soft glowing crescent holding a 3 on near-black is a calm night-light picture, but the tile is so dark it almost sinks into the dimmed home screen.

[#4]'s night sky with a moon and stars over purple hills also matches the sleep row ('Sleep Sounds - R...', 'Sleep Sounds Whi...'). Its '4' is tiny and nearly gone at the smallest tinted size, and on the home screen its name is cut to 'Paint by Mo...'.

[#1]: a single crescent with a small numeral 3 tucked inside it, on navy by day and near-black by night. The sky is only hinted at, one moon and nothing else, and the night version deepens on time without changing what it is.

[#4] is the only icon you can tell the hour from: a crescent, a few small stars and dusky hills, the sky hinted rather than announced; but its numeral 4 is a speck at home-screen size and vanishes in the smallest tinted icon, so it reads as a sleep app, not a painting one.
B and D shorten to "Moonlight" under the icon, which fits cleanly, while the full "Paint by Moonlight" stands apart from every rival name, all of which say "Paint/Color by Number".

[#4]: a picture-book night, with a smiling crescent glow, gold stars and soft purple hills. On the dimmed bedtime screen it is the one a child would ask to see again, but its 4 is so small it almost vanishes, and the label cuts off at 'Paint by Mo...'.

[#4]: the numeral 4 is tiny at the largest size and is just a speck at the smallest, so in one-color tint the icon reads as a night landscape and no longer says paint by numbers. Someone with low vision gets no clue about what the app does.

[#2] gives the numeral the most room and the 6 is the largest, plainest mark of all four, but the gold sliver on the left edge is a second accent that pulls the eye off it. 'Paint by Heart' fits whole under the icon.
[#4]: the home-screen name is cut to "Paint by Mo...", and its tiny 4 nearly vanishes at the smallest tinted size, so it reads as a landscape wallpaper, not a paint-by-number app.

[#4]: a little night scene with stars, a gold crescent and soft purple hills reads like a bedtime picture book, the warmest and safest icon here; but its 4 is tiny and the name truncates to "Paint by Mo...".
All four dark-background icons sink into the dimmed home screen next to the bright neighbors, so only the moon shapes in [#1] and [#4] catch the eye at night.

[#1]: the crescent with its "3" stays clear at every tinted size and in the dimmed view, but it looks like the crescents in the Sleep sounds row (White Noise, Sleep Sounds), so it reads more as a sleep app than a painting app.

[#1]: one cream crescent with a big friendly 3, plain and warm like a night-light. It stays clear at the smallest tinted size, though it sits very close to the sleep apps' crescents (White Noise, Sleep Sounds).
No candidate resembles the paint-by-number field, where nearly every icon is a lush flower, pixel heart or pumpkin with outlined numbered cells; the calm flat palettes alone stand apart there.
[#3]: the full moon's dark blotches read as stains rather than a face or craters at the smallest size, and the 4 is lost in them; less calm than the others.
[#2]: the dark hilltop band goes almost black in night mode, so it needs a warmer, mossier green to keep its cozy daytime feel after dark.
[#1] home-screen name 'Moonlight' drops the word 'Paint'; the label alone no longer says what the app does, so the icon's 3 must carry it.
B, C and D share one name, so the icon alone must carry the difference; the plainest one (D or C) carries it best.

[#2]'s big serif '6' on cream hills looks like no other icon in any row, and its numeral survives the tinted view at every size. But the name 'Paint by Heart' sits close to rival names like 'Paint Your World' and 'Happy Color'.
[#2]'s big "6" on a hill says numbers plainly, but nothing in it says night or wonder, and "Paint by Heart" reads warmly yet tells you less than the picture does.

[#1], [#3] and [#4] look the same on the day and night screens, with only the tile darkening. Their identity holds across modes, while [#2] flips from a cream ground to a dark one and looks like a different icon.

[#2]: the big serif 6 is the boldest numeral in the set and survives every size and the two-tone reduction, so it says 'numbers' best; but in tinted and dimmed views the hills read as a blank card, and the name Paint by Heart says nothing about photos or night.
[#4]: its home-screen name is cut to "Paint by Mo...", and its tiny "4" can't be read at night brightness or at the smallest tinted size, so neither the name nor the numbers come through.
All four stand apart from the busy, saturated flower-and-heart icons of the paint-by-number category; the calm night palette is distinctive there, though it borrows the sleep category's look.
[#2]'s hills-and-number scene has no link to its name 'Heart'. The icon and the name tell two different stories.
[#3]'s blotchy full moon looks more like a stained cookie than a moon at small sizes, and at night its dark purple spots make the face look bruised rather than gentle.
[#1]: the crescent and the 3 share one shape cleanly, but the horizon cuts the square in half and its ragged dithered edge is noise; the crescent alone on dark would be enough.
[#1]: flat fills, one even-weight ink stroke and a serif 3 make a clean crescent, but the perfect geometric arcs read as factory-precise rather than hand-grown.
[#2]: a single hill and a large bold 6 — the clearest numeral of the four, but the hill alone says landscape, not painting, and the name drops the moon the others share.
Every name reads as a gentle, welcoming sentence aloud ("I've been painting in ... every evening"); none scolds or excludes, and all four sit comfortably for a grandmother or a teenager.
[#2]: the large 6 under a hill line is the clearest numeral of the four at every size, but nothing in it says night or heart, so the icon and the name "Paint by Heart" don't tell one story.
[#2]: a single hill line and a single numeral, the plainest of the four, but the faint specks along the left of the sky are leftovers that should go.
[#3]: the full moon covered in purple blotches looks bruised or spotty rather than painted, which is less cozy than the others; the 4 is small and the icon nearly vanishes into the dark screen.

[#2]: thick uneven ink outlines and a hand-cut wavy hill edge feel drawn, but the 6 is so large it gets cropped in both views, so the numeral works as a wall rather than a label you could paint inside.
[#4]: the 4 sits tiny at the bottom edge, under two filled wave bands, so the one element that says 'paint by numbers' is the first to vanish at home-screen size.
None of the four has anything green or growing except [#2]'s teal hill. In the dimmed bedtime view [#3] and [#1] fade into flat dark tiles, while [#2]'s cream ground still glows warm.
In the tinted rendering every icon is the same amber on brown, so contrast does all the work: [#2] has the biggest light area and holds up best, while [#4]'s thin stars disappear.
[#4]: four stars, a dot field, a moon, three hill bands and a small 4 all in one square; take away the stars and dots and the numeral, now the smallest thing in the icon, might finally be seen.
[#4]'s home-screen name is cut to "Paint by Mo..." on both screens, losing the very word that carries the hour; it needs the short name "Moonlight" as [#1] and [#3] use.
None of them reaches for zodiac clip art or tarot kitsch, which is right; the gentlest sign of the sky is [#4]'s single bright star, the one small sign where a sign helps.
[#3]: the lumpy, uneven purple blobs look like moss or clouds dabbed on with a sponge, the most hand-grown texture here, and the thin serif 4 sits on them like a handwritten label in an herbal.

[#3] fills the moon with purple blots that crowd the 4; in the hedge crop the numeral is half-hidden under them, two things where one would do. In the two-tone view the blots vanish and only a plain disc with a 4 remains, which shows they were ornament.
[#1]: the crescent cradling its 3 stays clear at all three sizes, the cosmic and the cozy in one calm shape; the numeral is still readable at the smallest size.

[#1]: a white crescent on a dark navy square is the sleep row's common look (Sleep Sounds - R..., Sleep: Sounds & ..., Sleep Sounds Whi...). The numeral 3 is the only thing that sets it apart, so at a glance it reads as a sleep app, not as our own.
All four are dark tiles on a dark screen; only [#4] carries enough light and color to be found again at bedtime.
[#4]: the hills and sky are smooth airbrushed gradients with a soft glow around the moon, so up close it reads as polished digital render rather than something painted by hand; it leans slick.

[#4]: the 4 is tiny at the bottom and vanishes at the smallest tinted size and at phone size, so the icon stops saying 'by numbers' and becomes a generic night landscape like the Sleep Sounds icons; its name is also truncated to 'Paint by Mo...' on the home screen.
[#2]: the night version keeps the bold 6 and the gold wedge still bright, so it is starlit and plain together; the name 'Paint by Heart' fits whole but says nothing about the sky.
[#2] "Paint by Heart" has no sky in it at all: hills and a big 6, with no sun or moon, so nothing in it keeps the hours; it is legible and plain but it isn't mine to love.
None of the four carries anything a family would hesitate to hand a child; they are all kind and quiet, which is the right temperature for a bedtime app.

[#4]: the gradient sky, glowing moon and layered purple hills are the slickest of the four, and its '4' is a tiny speck at home-screen size. On the home screen the name is cut to 'Paint by Mo...', which loses the moonlight it is named for.

[#1]: a crescent with a 3 sits right beside the sleep-sounds row (White Noise, Sleep Sounds, Sleep: Sounds & ...) in the originality sheet; the outlined moon as a paintable region is the only cue that it isn't a sleep app.
None of the four names repeats a rival's naming pattern: every rival listed is 'X: Paint by Number' or a coined brand, and none uses 'Paint by <noun>'. No franchise, order or house name appears.
[#1]: the crescent outline survives at every size, but the 3 sits inside the curve and gets very small at the smallest size. Making it larger would fix that.

[#4]: crescent, gold stars and purple hills is the whole night sky drawn out, which is more than a hint, and the 4 almost disappears at this size. It also looks exactly the same on the day screen as on the night screen, so you can't tell the hour from it, and its name is cut to 'Paint by Mo...'.
Every icon already has a numeral and a sky; the ones that keep only those two, [#2] and [#3], read at once, while [#4] fills every silence.

[#1]: a plain crescent holding a bold 3 is a quiet companion and survives two-tone and the smallest tinted size, but in the originality row it sits close to the sleep apps' white crescents (White Noise, Sleep Sounds), so the moon alone doesn't say painting.
[#4]: the numeral 4 is a tiny speck at the bottom; at the smallest tinted size it vanishes, so the icon reads as a generic night landscape, and its home-screen label is truncated to "Paint by Mo...".
[#2]: the big 6 under a dark hill with only a sliver of orange sun feels like dusk turning to dark, more lonely than cozy, and nothing in it twinkles.

[#1]: a lone crescent on dark navy sits very close to the sleep row (Sleep Sounds - R..., Sleep: Sounds & ..., White Noise Deep...); the numeral 3 is the only thing setting it apart, and it shrinks to a speck at the smallest tinted size. Not a franchise copy, but the look is the sleep category's, not ours.
[#2]: the big "6" is the boldest numeral and reads at every size. But the dunes and the name "Paint by Heart" say nothing about night or photos, so it is the least distinct of the four.
All four keep the bottom third of the tile empty or light, so the icons look cut off; the frame's lower edge could go consistently or be closed.

[#3]: one large disc and one numeral, with dark space all around; little is left to take away, though the thin crescent line under the disc and the dithered lower edge are a second moon where one would do.

[#2]: no rival name contains "Heart" with "Paint by", though heart icons are common among color-by-number rivals (Color by Number, Colors by Number, Sandbox); its icon uses dunes and a 6, not a heart, so no look-alike.
[#2]: the black outline wobbles and swells along the hill, like an inked line drawn with a brush, and the cream area has a faint paper-like warmth, so it feels drawn rather than extruded.
[#1]: a crescent with a small 3 on a navy tile tells you it's night at a glance and only hints at the sky. But the 3 is tiny, and nothing in the tile says paint.
[#4]: the name cuts off to 'Paint by Mo...' under the icon, so the moonlight part of the name, the part a child would say, is lost.
[#4]: stars, a smiling crescent and purple hills over a white page make a little picture-book bedtime scene, the warmest and brightest tile in the row; the 4 is tiny though.
[#3]: the outlined full moon with purple patches reads as paintable regions and keeps its 4 legible at mid size; in two tones the patches vanish entirely, leaving only a disc and a numeral.
[#1]: flat navy and cream with a perfectly even, compass-drawn outline; clean and legible, but geometric and cool, closer to a badge than a hand-colored page.
[#1]: the crescent's lower half dissolves into the light ground and survives only as a thin outline, so the dark band could go or be extended so the moon holds its shape.
None of the four slips into horoscope or zodiac kitsch; [#1], [#3] and [#4] only get darker at night, while [#2] actually tells day from night.

[#4] puts the stars, the crescent and the soft hills in one small picture, the cosmic and the cozy side by side, but its tiny "4" is gone at the smallest tinted size and its home-screen name is cut to "Paint by Mo...", so under the icon it never finishes saying what it is.
[#2]: a large numeral 6 over cream and green hill bands looks like no competitor's icon. 'Paint by Heart' echoes no rival name shown, though it moves away from the moon theme of the other three.
[#1]'s crescent cradling a "3" stays clear at all three tinted sizes and in the dimmed bedtime view, and "Moonlight" fits under it whole: calm, no fuss, a picture any child can read.

[#4]: smooth airbrushed gradients in the sky, hills and moon, with a soft vignette, read as stock vector rendering; only the ink line and serif 4 at the bottom right hint at a painted template, so the center crop could belong to any wallpaper app.
[#3]: the moon's dark blotches crowd the 4, and at the smallest size the numeral merges into the craters, so the icon blurs into a textured circle.

[#2]: the 6 is the largest, clearest numeral of the four and survives the smallest tinted size, but the dark teal sky nearly vanishes into the dark home screen and the name 'Paint by Heart' says nothing about photos or numbers.
[#4]: stars, moon, three hills and a tiny 4 crowd the square; the 4 is the smallest element and sits at the very bottom, so the stars could go and the numeral would read.
[#3]: the moon's purple blotches read as craters or stains rather than painted regions, and in the bedtime-dimmed view the dark tile nearly merges with the dark screen, leaving a floating disc.

[#3]: the full moon is painted in purple numbered patches, the only icon that says 'paint by number' about the moon itself. In dark mode its tile goes near-black and the moon carries the icon on its own.

[#3]: a full moon with purple paint-blob maria and a tiny 4 reads as a moon by day and by night. But the numeral is faint and the blobs make it look more like a cookie or a palette than a sky, so the hour is less legible than in [#1].

[#1]: crescent plus a 3 sitting inside it is the simplest silhouette and holds up at all three tinted sizes and in two tones, but a dark tile with a white crescent sits squarely among the Sleep sounds rivals (White Noise, Sleep Sounds), so it can read as a sleep app.
All: none of them looks like the busy flower and pixel-heart icons the rivals use, and A–C share the "Moonlight" name, which none of the listed rival names come close to.
[#2]: the large 6 is clear and kind, but the dark teal sky and black hill read as a gloomy dusk on the dark screen, and nothing in the picture says 'heart'.

[#1]: the outlined crescent with a big serif 3 inside reads as 'numbered region' at every tinted size, but a lone crescent on navy sits right beside the Sleep sounds row (White Noise, Sleep Sounds), so it risks looking like a sleep app.
[#3]: a full moon with a painted numeral 4 on deep purple matches no rival in any row. The full moon looks a little like BetterSleep's, but the paint blotches and numeral make it distinct.
[#2]: the big 6 is the clearest number of all, but the dark green-black hills feel cold and the name "Paint by Heart" breaks the moon/night story the others share.
All four names sound natural when spoken in a sentence and nothing in them scolds the user. 'Moonlight' does hint at evening painting, but it doesn't exclude anyone.
[#4]: the name is cut to 'Paint by Mo...' on both screens, so the home screen loses the word that gives the hour.

[#2]: the big 6 is the most legible numeral, but the dunes carry no moon or star, so the picture doesn't hold the night the other names promise; "Paint by Heart" is warm and kind, though it pairs with an icon that doesn't show a heart.

[#3]'s full moon with blotchy patches that look like paint regions is the one moon in the pack no sleep or meditation rival has, and it hints at a painted template. On the home screen its label shortens cleanly to 'Moonlight'.
[#3], [#4], [#1] share 'Paint by Moonlight', which no rival name resembles, while every rival name leans on 'Paint by Number'; the name is owned, the icon has to carry the painting.
[#4]: a night sky with crescent and stars over purple hills reads like the sleep row (Sleep Sounds - R..., Sleep Sounds Whi...), and its tiny '4' is nearly invisible, so it says sleep before paint.

[#3]: the moon's purple blobs are drawn in round, lumpy shapes like moss or lichen on a stone, and the inked rim keeps it homely. But in the two-tone view the blobs vanish and it becomes a plain white disc with a 4, so the handmade texture doesn't hold up.
[#4]: in the two-tone view the moon breaks into a ragged blob and its gradients turn to noise; the soft night scene sits right among the sleep-sound icons.
